newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bourse trade limit delay not welcomed.
newsitem.headline: Thai bourse trade limit delay not welcomed.

text.p: A decision by the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) to postpone widening the daily trading limit on common shares to 30 percent from 10 percent will hurt retail investors, analysts said on Friday.
The SET said on Wednesday that the 30 percent daily trading range limit on common shares, originally to come into effect on Friday, was postponed for an indefinite period.
No reasons for the decision and no date for the change have been given.
Analysts said the postponement meant retail investors, who bought in anticipation that the higher limits would fuel higher profits, would instead unload stocks soon in order to avoid further losses.
"The postponement will hurt investors," said Barry Yates, head of regional research with Seamico Securities. He said they may find it hard to offload stocks if the market drops.
"You have flexibility with the 30 percent," he said.
Broker members of the exchange voted just after the baht was floated on July 2 to widen the trading band.
After the baht float many stocks hit their 10 percent daily ceilings early in the trading day and many orders could not be completed. The widening was meant to free up trading and add liquidity.
But some have criticised the timing of the measure, saying it could bring more volatility to the market just as Thailand is struggling to handle a severe economic crisis.
Chetta Meemangkang, analyst at Prime Finance and Securities, said Thailand needed 30 percent trading limits because several neighbouring countries had already adopted more flexible trading limits.

"The widening of the trading limit would force retail investors to think harder in future before they move to sell or buy. Out of the total investors, some 60 percent are local retail investors and they hardly use market fundamentals before trading," said Chetta.

Analysts said they believed a new date to increase the trading limit would probably be announced following talks next week between International Monetary Fund (IMF) and Thai officials on ways to tackle Thailand's economic problems.
Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya is expected to present results of the talks to a weekly cabinet meeting on Tuesday.

"The timing obviously concerns the market. The market is hopeful that an accommodation will be reached with the IMF. But if no agreement is forthcoming next week then the market will be sold off sharply," Yates said.
